item.title: Phoenix tried a reflective coating on black asphalt; noon surface heat fell 12°F
item.description:
📝 Rather than plain black asphalt, the city painted some roads with a light-colored, reflective coating, on the theory that a lighter road would keep cooler. The catch nobody expectedA cooler road doesn’t necessarily mean a cooler walk. The reflective coating reflects more sunlight than it absorbs, which helps keep the surface cooler.
🔗 Read more: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/phoenix-swapped-black-asphalt-for-a-reflective-road-coating-noon-surface-heat-fell-12f-but-pedestrians-faced-higher-radiant-heat/articleshow/133421891.cms?from=mdr

item.title: 远程工作挑战：来自 5 个城市的经验教训
item.description:
📝 Topics: Build Communities +1 Strengthen State Government Projects: State Fiscal Policy The Remote Work Challenge: Lessons From 5 Cities As office building vacancies jeopardize urban fiscal health and downtown vitality, here’s how cities and states are adapting The Pew Charitable Trusts Report May 13, 2026 The Remote Work Challenge: Lessons From 5 Cities (PDF) SHARE Downloads The Remote Work Challenge: Lessons From 5 Cities (PDF) Overview The COVID-19 pandemic called into question the economic vitality of U. Each city was selected because at least some data points suggested it might be vulnerable to economic and fiscal challenges from remote work. The effects of remote work on cities have been manageable so far, but city leaders should be concerned that they are not happening in isolation: Cities are also struggling with rising costs, reduced state and federal support, and fragile economies, among other challenges.
🔤 Original: The Remote Work Challenge: Lessons from 5 Cities
